_description: This is a comprehensive template showing all available configuration options for Synteles Agentlet. Copy and customize this file for your use case. Note: Fields starting with '_' are documentation and will be ignored by the parser.

_environment_variables.description: Required environment variables depend on your model provider

_secrets_description: List of secret names owned by this agentlet's creator (optional). Platform-only field — agentlet-core silently ignores it; secrets are injected into the environment before the process starts. Each entry is a plain secret name (string) — not an ARN or path. At runtime the Synteles Platform resolves each name relative to the agentlet owner's UserId and injects the values. Example: ['anthropic-keys', 'database-credentials']

agentlet._description: Agentlet metadata - basic information about your agentlet
agentlet.name: my-agentlet

prompt: Analyze the project structure and provide insights
_prompt_description: Default user prompt/task for the agentlet to execute. Can be overridden via CLI with --prompt flag. If not provided here, --prompt must be specified on command line.
system_prompt:
You are a helpful AI assistant specialized in software development.

Your capabilities:
- Analyze code and provide insights
- Execute bash commands to inspect the system
- Read and write files
- Search documentation

Always:
- Be concise and accurate
- Explain your reasoning
- Ask for clarification when needed
- Prioritize security and best practices
_system_prompt_description: Instructions that define the agentlet's behavior, personality, and capabilities. This is sent to the LLM as the system message.

model._provider_description: Model provider (required). Supported: anthropic, bedrock, openai, azure, vertex_ai, and any LiteLLM provider. See: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers
model._model_id_description: Model identifier (required). Format varies by provider.

parameters._description: Model-specific parameters (optional). These are passed directly to the LLM API.

_additional_options.stop_sequences: Array of custom stop sequences, e.g., ['END']

retry._description: Retry configuration for handling transient errors (optional). Helps handle rate limits, API timeouts, and connection errors.
retry._initial_retry_interval_description: Initial retry interval in seconds (default: 30.0). First retry waits this long after failure.
retry._backoff_factor_description: Exponential backoff factor (default: 2.0). Each retry interval = previous interval * backoff_factor. Example: 30s, 60s, 120s, 240s with factor 2.0
retry._max_retry_interval_description: Maximum retry interval in seconds (default: 300.0). Caps the exponential backoff to prevent excessively long waits.
retry._retry_on_errors_description: List of error types to retry on (optional). Default list includes common transient errors. Add custom error types as needed.

_tools_description: Built-in tools from strands-agents-tools package (imported as strands_tools.<name>). Common tools: shell (execute shell commands), editor (advanced file editing), file_read (read files), file_write (write files), use_computer (keyboard/mouse/screenshots), http_request, tavily, python_repl, calculator, environment, current_time, use_llm, workflow, batch, think, swarm. Tools are loaded on-demand; consent is auto-granted via BYPASS_TOOL_CONSENT=true.

mcp_tools._description: STDIO SERVER EXAMPLE - Launches MCP server as subprocess with stdin/stdout communication
mcp_tools.name: filesystem
mcp_tools._server_description: Server transport type (required). Options: stdio, http, sse
mcp_tools._env_description: Environment variables for the subprocess. ${WORK_DIR} will be replaced with the working directory.
mcp_tools._prefix_description: Tool name prefix (optional). Prevents naming conflicts when using multiple MCP servers. Example: 'read_file' becomes 'fs_read_file'

tool_filters._description: Control which tools from this server are loaded (optional)
tool_filters._allowed_description: Only load these specific tools (mutually exclusive with 'rejected')
tool_filters._rejected_description: Or use 'rejected' to exclude specific tools (mutually exclusive with 'allowed')

mcp_tools._description: HTTP (STREAMABLE) SERVER EXAMPLE - Connects to MCP server via HTTP with streaming support
mcp_tools.name: web-search
mcp_tools._api_key_env_description: Environment variable containing API key (optional). Will be added as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' header if not already present.

mcp_tools._description: SSE (Server-Sent Events) SERVER EXAMPLE - Connects to MCP server via SSE for real-time event streaming
mcp_tools.name: realtime-data
mcp_tools._note: SSE client currently doesn't support custom headers. Include authentication in the URL or handle server-side. api_key_env is ignored for SSE servers.

_mcp_tools_description: Model Context Protocol tools integration. Supports stdio (subprocess), HTTP (streamable), and SSE (Server-Sent Events). MCP servers provide additional tools and capabilities to the agent.
_sub_agentlets_description: SUB-AGENTLETS (optional) — Transform this agentlet into an orchestrator by declaring inline sub-agentlets. Each becomes a callable tool the orchestrator's LLM can invoke. Sub-agentlets run in-process (no subprocess/IPC). Key rules: name must be unique (becomes tool name); description is what the orchestrator LLM reads to decide when to call it; system_prompt defines specialisation; model is optional (inherits orchestrator's model when omitted); tools/mcp_tools follow the same schema as top-level; output defaults to all-false (silent). No resource_limits or nested sub_agentlets per sub-agentlet.

_sub_agentlets_example.name: research_agent
_sub_agentlets_example._name_note: Unique identifier — becomes the tool name the orchestrator calls
_sub_agentlets_example.description: Searches for factual information on a given topic and returns a concise summary with key findings and sources. Use for any task requiring up-to-date information or fact-checking.
_sub_agentlets_example._description_note: What the orchestrator LLM reads to decide when to call this sub-agentlet. Be specific — start with a verb.
_sub_agentlets_example.system_prompt: You are a research specialist. Find accurate, up-to-date information on the given topic. Return a structured summary: key findings, supporting details, and sources. Be concise.
_sub_agentlets_example._model_note: No model key — inherits the orchestrator's model

output._output_note: All false by default (silent). Set to true to see this sub-agentlet's execution inline.

_sub_agentlets_example.name: writing_agent
_sub_agentlets_example.description: Transforms research notes, bullet points, or raw information into well-structured written content. Use after research_agent has gathered the necessary information.
_sub_agentlets_example.system_prompt: You are a professional writer. Transform research notes into clear, well-structured content. Use headings and logical structure. Synthesise — do not just restate bullet points.

model._model_note: Override the orchestrator's model — useful for cost optimisation

_swarm_description: SWARM (optional) — Run a set of specialised agents that hand off directly to each other with no central coordinator, powered by strands.multiagent.Swarm. Three modes: Declarative (define participants in a 'swarm' key), Dynamic (add 'swarm' to the tools list), or Combined (both). IMPORTANT: 'swarm' and 'sub_agentlets' are mutually exclusive. Name expansion: count=1 → name unchanged; count>1 → name_1, name_2, … Entry point defaults to the first participant's first instance.

_swarm_example._entry_point_description: Base name of the participant that receives the initial prompt. Defaults to the first participant.
_swarm_example._max_handoffs_description: Maximum total handoffs before the swarm halts (default: 20)
_swarm_example._execution_timeout_description: Total swarm wall-clock limit in seconds, enforced by the Strands SDK (default: 900). Set this in the swarm block — NOT via --timeout. The --timeout flag is an independent outer process ceiling and should be set to match or exceed this value.
_swarm_example._node_timeout_description: Per-agent turn limit in seconds, enforced by the Strands SDK (default: 300). Prevents one agent from blocking the panel indefinitely.
_swarm_example._repetitive_handoff_min_unique_agents_de: Min unique agents required in detection window (default: 0 = disabled)

participants.name: solutions_architect
participants.description: Designs architecture and evaluates technical trade-offs. Use for system design, technology selection, and integration patterns.
participants.system_prompt: You are a senior solutions architect on an expert panel. Design systems, evaluate trade-offs, and produce clear recommendations. Hand off to devops_engineer for infrastructure concerns.
participants._model_note: Omit 'model' to inherit the top-level model; specify to override per participant
participants._mcp_tools_note: mcp_tools follows the same schema as top-level mcp_tools

participants.name: devops_engineer
participants._count_note: count=1: name stays as devops_engineer (no _N suffix)
participants.description: Handles infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and operational concerns. Use for deployment strategies, monitoring, scaling, and reliability topics.
participants.system_prompt: You are a senior DevOps engineer on an expert panel. Address infrastructure, deployment, and reliability concerns with concrete, implementable guidance.

model._model_note: Override to use a cheaper model for lower-complexity roles

resource_limits._description: Constraints on agentlet execution to prevent runaway token costs and tool loops. Timeout model: singleton/sub-agentlet — set execution timeout at launch via --timeout flag, do NOT add max_execution_time here; swarm — use swarm.execution_timeout and swarm.node_timeout (Strands SDK-enforced), with --timeout as an independent outer ceiling.
resource_limits._max_tokens_description: Maximum tokens for LLM generation (default: 10000). Includes both input and output tokens. Can be overridden via CLI with --max-tokens flag.
resource_limits._max_tool_calls_description: Maximum number of tool calls allowed (default: 20). Prevents infinite loops of tool invocations.

output._format_description: Output format (default: 'markdown'). Options: 'markdown', 'json', 'text'. Can be overridden via CLI with --output-format flag.
output._show_messages_description: Show complete assistant messages per turn (default: true). When true: displays full response text from the agent. When false: only shows metadata and tool calls.
output._show_reasoning_description: Show agent reasoning steps (default: true). Displays the LLM's extended thinking/reasoning blocks. Only shown when model supports reasoning (e.g., Claude with extended thinking).
output._show_tool_calls_description: Show tool invocations (default: true). Displays when tools are called with their parameters and results.
output._show_turn_boundaries_description: Show turn boundaries in multi-turn conversations (default: false). When true: displays visual separators between conversation turns. Useful for debugging multi-turn agent interactions.

observability._description: OpenTelemetry integration for traces and metrics export. Enables comprehensive observability for production deployments.

otel._enabled_description: Enable OpenTelemetry trace export (default: false). When enabled, traces are sent to OTLP endpoint.
otel._otlp_endpoint_description: OTLP base endpoint URL (optional). Used as fallback if signal-specific endpoints not set. OpenTelemetry will automatically append /v1/traces and /v1/metrics. Defaults to http://localhost:4318 or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT env var.
otel._otlp_traces_endpoint_description: Signal-specific endpoint for traces (optional). Overrides otlp_endpoint for traces. OpenTelemetry automatically appends /v1/traces.
otel._otlp_metrics_endpoint_description: Signal-specific endpoint for metrics (optional). Overrides otlp_endpoint for metrics. OpenTelemetry automatically appends /v1/metrics.
otel._otlp_headers_description: Custom headers sent with OTLP requests (optional). Example for Langfuse: {'Authorization': 'Bearer your-langfuse-secret-key'}
otel._console_exporter_description: Prints trace spans to stdout for development/debugging (default: false). Useful for verifying traces are being generated correctly.
otel._sampler_description: Trace sampler type (optional). Controls which traces get exported to reduce volume/cost. Options: always_on (export all traces, good for development), always_off (export no traces), traceidratio (export a percentage based on sampler_arg), parentbased_always_on (follow parent span's sampling decision).
otel._sampler_arg_description: Sampler argument (optional). For traceidratio sampler: percentage to export (0.0 to 1.0). Example: 0.1 = 10% of traces (useful for high-volume production).
otel._enable_metrics_description: Enable metrics export (default: false). Export metrics in addition to traces. Provides quantitative performance data (latency, throughput, etc.).
otel._trace_attributes_description: Custom trace attributes (optional). Added to all trace spans for filtering/grouping. Useful for identifying service, environment, version, etc.

_notes.environment_variables: Environment variables can be referenced using ${VAR_NAME} or $VAR_NAME syntax. Special variable ${WORK_DIR} will be replaced with the working directory path.
_notes.litellm_providers: For a complete list of supported LLM providers and their configuration, see: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers
_notes.mcp_protocol: For more information about Model Context Protocol, see: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/
_notes.strands_tools: Built-in tools are from the strands-agents-tools package. Tool consent is auto-granted via BYPASS_TOOL_CONSENT=true.
